PATIENT: Lysander Fairfax Phone: 28451903 email:bradleymorgan@example.org DATE OF BIRTH: 1947-05-12 AGE: 80 years
FOLLOW-UP DATE: 06/09/28 FOLLOWED BY: Dr. Emily Carter
CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit for COPD management, persistent bilateral lower extremity edema, and mental health evaluation.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. Lysander Fairfax returns for follow-up approximately six weeks after his last visit. He reports that his respiratory status has slightly improved with the increased use of his albuterol inhaler, now averaging three to four times daily. He continues to experience wheezing, particularly at night, but notes fewer episodes of dyspnea during exertion. Mr. Fairfax has been compliant with his inhaler regimen, and he reports that the addition of pulmonary rehabilitation has been beneficial in managing his symptoms.
The bilateral lower extremity edema remains a significant concern. Mr. Fairfax describes the swelling as persistent and worsening, particularly at the end of the day, rating the discomfort as an 8/10 on the pain scale. He has adhered to dietary sodium restrictions and has been diligent in monitoring his fluid intake; however, the edema has not improved significantly. He reports difficulty with ambulation and increased discomfort when standing for prolonged periods.
In terms of mental health, Mr. Fairfax expresses that although he has been attending therapy sessions, he still experiences heightened anxiety, particularly following the recent passing of a close friend. He reports episodes of insomnia and feelings of restlessness, leading to increased fatigue during the day. He has been utilizing coping strategies discussed in therapy but feels the need for additional support.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
General - + increased fatigue, no fevers or chills. Pulmonary - + dyspnea on exertion, + wheezing, - cough, - sputum production, no hemoptysis. Cardiac - no chest pain or palpitations, + orthopnea. Gastrointestinal - no nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. Musculoskeletal - + joint pain, + worsening bilateral lower extremity edema. Neurological - + increased anxiety, + insomnia, no dizziness or headaches.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) 2. Hypertension 3. Osteoarthritis 4. Persistent fatigue 5. Anxiety and depression (ongoing management)
PAST SURGICAL HISTORY
1. Right knee arthroscopy in 2018.
FAMILY HISTORY
Father - history of lung cancer. Mother - history of hypertension.
SOCIAL HISTORY
Lives alone in , . Former carpenter, now retired. Quit smoking 15 years ago. Occasional alcohol use. No illicit drug use.
ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.
MEDICATIONS ON FOLLOW-UP
1. Albuterol inhaler as needed, currently using three to four times daily. 2. Lisinopril 20 mg daily. 3. Fluticasone/salmeterol 500/50 MDI, 2 puffs twice daily. 4. Tiotropium 18 mcg inhaler, 2 puffs daily. 5. Acetaminophen 500 mg as needed for pain. 6. Furosemide 160 mg daily (no change). 7. Sertraline 150 mg daily (no change).
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: T 98.7F, HR 76, BP 128/82, RR 20, O2 sat 82% on room air.
General: Elderly male in mild respiratory distress, appears fatigued but engaged. HEENT: No nasal congestion, oropharynx clear. Pulmonary: Diminished breath sounds bilaterally, moderate wheezing noted on expiration, no crackles. Cardiac: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmurs. Extremities: 4+ pitting edema in bilateral lower extremities, no erythema or warmth.
LABORATORY DATA
1. CBC: WBC 8.9, Hgb 10.5, Hct 31.0, Plt 210. 2. BMP: Na 132, K 4.1, Cl 99, CO2 26, BUN 40, Cr 2.4, Glucose 90. 3. BNP: 620 (slight decrease). 4. Thyroid function tests: TSH 2.3 (within normal limits).
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. COPD management: Mr. Fairfax's respiratory symptoms have shown slight improvement with increased adherence to inhaler therapy and pulmonary rehabilitation. Continue current inhalers and encourage consistent participation in rehabilitation. A follow-up pulmonary function test is recommended in one month to assess lung function. 2. Hypertension: Continue lisinopril. Blood pressure remains stable. Follow-up in 1 month. 3. Lower extremity edema: The edema persists despite furosemide therapy. A referral to nephrology is warranted for further evaluation of renal function and optimization of diuretic therapy. Reinforce dietary sodium restrictions and encourage daily weight monitoring. 4. Mental health: Due to persistent anxiety levels, Mr. Fairfax will continue with sertraline at 150 mg daily. A follow-up with psychiatry is scheduled in two weeks for ongoing management and reassessment of treatment efficacy. Explore additional therapeutic options such as mindfulness-based stress reduction to address anxiety and insomnia.
Patient education reiterated regarding the importance of recognizing exacerbation signs, adherence to medication, and lifestyle modifications to effectively manage COPD and edema.
